output.headline: Allows board and district committees to keep meeting virtually in February 2022
output.summary: This resolution makes the findings state law requires so that the board and other district public bodies subject to the Brown Act (California's open meeting law) can hold virtual meetings during February 2022. It involves no spending.

output.headline: Ratifies $2,500 for English classes for parents at East Oakland Pride Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $2,500.00

output.summary: The district would pay a contractor up to $2,500 to teach English as a Second Language classes to 25-30 parents, twice a week for 16 weeks, at East Oakland Pride Elementary School. The service period is January 24 to March 25, 2022, and the work began before the board's approval. The money comes from Title I, a federal grant for low-income students.

output.headline: Approves up to $400,000 for The Unity Council to run child care and development programs

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $400,000.00

output.summary: The board would pass a portion of the district's 2021-22 state child development funding, up to $400,000, to the Spanish Speaking Unity Council of Alameda County (doing business as The Unity Council) through a subcontract. The period is July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2022. It is part of the district's early childhood education programs.

output.headline: Pays Spearitwurx up to $97,500 for equity and wellness work with school staff

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $97,500.00

output.summary: The district would pay Spearitwurx, an Oakland provider, up to $97,500 through the Office of Equity. The work includes staff assessments, school site visits, 5-7 customized sessions (15 hours in total), wellness kits and coaching for selected staff. The service period is January 3 to June 30, 2022, which began before the January 26 board meeting.

output.headline: Finds charter schools cannot be housed at a single district site for 2022-23
output.summary: This resolution makes a finding, with a written statement of reasons, that the charter schools requesting facilities cannot be accommodated at a single school site. It relates to charter school facilities requests for the 2022-2023 school year.

output.headline: Leases the Ascend campus to Ascend Charter School for two years, expecting $216,367 in 2022-23

money.evidence: Anticipated revenue to the District of $216,367.00 in 2022-23

output.summary: The district would let Ascend Charter School use the Ascend Campus (44,704 square feet) from July 1, 2022 to June 30, 2024 under an in-lieu of Proposition 39 agreement. The charter school pays the state-set per-square-foot rate in 2022-23 and 1.05 times that rate in 2023-24. The district expects $216,367 in revenue in 2022-23.

output.headline: Leases 2111 International Blvd to Community School for Creative Education, expecting $126,351

money.evidence: Anticipated revenue to the District of $126,351.00 in 2022-23 (if elected)

output.summary: The district would let Community School for Creative Education, a charter school, use 2111 International Blvd for one year, July 1, 2022 to June 30, 2023, with an option for one more year through June 30, 2024. The school pays the state-set Proposition 39 per-square-foot rate on 17,870 square feet and two times that rate on 3,994 square feet. The district expects $126,351 in 2022-23 revenue, noted in the text as if the option is elected.

output.headline: Leases Toler Heights campus to Francophone Charter School, expecting $35,922 in 2022-23

money.evidence: Anticipated revenue to the District of $35,922.00 in 2022-23

output.summary: The district would let Francophone Charter School use the Toler Heights Campus (7,422 square feet) from July 1, 2022 to June 30, 2024 under an in-lieu of Proposition 39 agreement. The school pays the state-set per-square-foot rate in 2022-23 and 1.05 times that rate in 2023-24. The district may adjust the fee if it provides routine repair, cleaning and maintenance, and expects $35,922 in 2022-23.

output.headline: Board votes on laying off classified staff for 2022-23 because of lack of funds or work
output.summary: This resolution would authorize a reduction in force, which means layoffs, of classified employees for the 2022-2023 fiscal year, citing lack of funds and/or lack of work. Classified employees are district staff who are not teachers or administrators. The text does not say which positions or how many are affected.

output.headline: Freezes hiring for school-site and central office positions starting January 27, 2022
output.summary: This resolution puts a temporary hiring freeze in place for positions at school sites and in the central office. It takes effect January 27, 2022. The text does not say how long the freeze lasts.

output.headline: Approves Castlemont High trip to Oregon college campuses at no cost to the district
output.summary: Castlemont High School would take 12 students and 3 adults to Eugene, Oregon, from January 31 to February 4, 2022. They would volunteer with Habitat for Humanity and tour Bushnell University, Lane Community College and the University of Oregon. The trip costs the district nothing.

output.summary: The board would approve the written minutes of its regular meeting held January 12, 2022. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting.
